source.notes: Intelligent plants are necessary to ensure maximum energy production and minimal maintenance. Existing wind plants are typically designed and operated to maximize energy production or minimize cost of energy, but structural loads and fatigue and their associated costs have traditionally been difficult to account for. Fortunately, advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning have opened up new opportunities to improve wind plant performance. This work considers impacts on damage equivalent loads (DELs), calculated using artificial neural network surrogate models, due to the positioning and operation of wind turbines. The models are trained on simulation data to predict four specific DELs: blade root bending moment, shaft bending moment, yaw bearing bending moment, and tower base bending moment. These DEL channels can be used to inform operating strategies for existing wind plants that reduce cost and increase efficiency. The trained surrogate models are integrated with a plant analysis tool to investigate the Pareto-optimal trade-off of maximizing energy production and minimizing plant land use area on the respective DELs. Our results follow expected trends between turbine positioning, annual energy production, and DELS, providing confidence in the newly integrated load surrogate models.
source.title: Impacts on Damage Equivalent Loads from Plant Optimization Using Artificial Neural Network Surrogate Models
